sections.title: The view (Wave A)
sections.note: The recommended option is built if you do not answer.

questions.q: How should the Topology View lay the devices out?
questions.why: You asked for left→right and top→down = upstream, mid, downstream. There are two readings of 'mid'.

opts.d: Column 0 Elosztó, then the boxes (deeper boxes of a string further right), then leader → … → tail. One horizontal lane per room, in the order the trunk reaches them. fig/02.
Column = number of hops from the Elosztó on the path graph, no room lanes. Shows depth honestly, but a room's devices scatter.
A classic tree diagram per circuit, Elosztó on the left. Clear per circuit, but the shared pathway (what you asked to see) disappears.

questions.q: Where does the Topology View open?
questions.why: It is a viewer mode, but you will switch back to the blueprint often.

opts.d: Over the canvas, Esc steps back to the blueprint; a mini-plan in the inspector and 'Mutasd az alaprajzon' flash the real path.
Blueprint and topology side by side, both live. Needs the layout system (05db) to host a second surface — larger.
Opens in a new tab with a copy of the project. No selection sync; edits must be carried back.

questions.q: Where does the autowiring playback run?
questions.why: The animation is clearest on the simple topology, but the real geometry is what gets built.

opts.d: Plays in the Topology View; a toggle 'Alaprajzon is' runs the same sequence along the real paths on the blueprint.
Simplest; the blueprint shows only the end result.
Plays on the drawing; the topology view just shows the composite.

sections.title: Rules (Wave B) — checkpoint T3
sections.note: These are trade rules. ⚑ = values to confirm.

questions.q: May a Kötődoboz / szobadoboz be the master (mini-Elosztó) of a SOCKET circuit?
questions.why: Your description says yes (a KD serving a room's szobadugalj circuits). The earlier E06 answer made socket circuits classic chains Elosztó → first socket → … and kept the szobadoboz out of socket distribution.

opts.d: Default stays the classic chain (E06); an explicit Master link from a box in the Topology View is honoured and the box becomes the room's mini-Elosztó.
Socket circuits always chain from the Elosztó; boxes only pass them through.
When a room has a KD / szobadoboz, its socket circuits start there automatically.

questions.q: A dedicated circuit passing a kötődoboz / portal box:
questions.why: Home runs often share the first stretch with others and pass the same boxes.

opts.d: It may pass through the box (or by it), the cable stays continuous from the Elosztó to the device.
Its path must not touch any box — can force longer routes.
May be jointed in a box like any other circuit.

questions.q: Switching in CHAIN mode: how does N reach the lamps? ⚑
questions.why: In a chain (master → switch → switch → lamp) the lamp needs N; either it travels through the switch boxes or it comes separately from the master.

opts.t: N + PE through the switch boxes
opts.d: master→S1 L·N·PE (3×1,5), S↔S T1·T2·N·PE (4×1,5), tail→lamp Lk·N·PE (3×1,5). Needs deep boxes and a connector for N. fig/05 left.
The switches carry only L / travellers; a separate Lk·N·PE cable goes master → lamp. More cable, simpler switch boxes.

questions.q: When is the STAR (common point) suggested for a switching group?
questions.why: You said the star is preferred when the common point coincides with the room's wall crossing (portal) point.

opts.d: Star via that portal box when at least two switches of the group sit at the same door; chain otherwise. You can always toggle.

opts.t: Always star when a portal box exists
opts.d: Even a single switch goes via the portal box.
Chain by default; star only by hand.

questions.q: May a socket chain branch at a socket?
questions.why: A T-branch from a socket box is common in practice but makes the 'leader → tail' sequence a tree.

opts.d: A socket has at most one chain link out; a branch needs a kötődoboz (two masters from it). fig/03 P4.
At most 2 chain links out of one socket box (≤ 3 conductors per terminal ⚑).

questions.q: Socket chain order: 'least horizontal movement' measured how?
questions.why: Two sockets on either side of a wall corner are close in a straight line but the cable goes round along the walls.

opts.d: Path length on the path graph (arc length along the Vezethető fal faces). fig/04.
Simpler, but can order sockets across a corner or a doorway the cable cannot take.

questions.q: A socket chain hop: arc from socket to socket, or through a leállás box?
questions.why: You described arcs: vertical up, along beside the gerinc, vertical down into the next socket. The E5 engine today puts a 2-gang leállás box at 2450 above every wall endpoint.

opts.d: Socket box → socket box in one pipe (up, along, down). A leállás box only where several devices drop together (≤ 250 mm) or where the circuit branches. Changes E5 counts — only for circuits with a topology (T12).
Every drop gets its 2-gang box at the distribution height, as E5 does now.

sections.title: Sharing and the engine (Wave C)
sections.note: Checkpoint T10 shows these on CLA before T12.

questions.q: The V1 house string (Elosztó → KD → KD …): own conduit?
questions.why: You wrote 'in their own (often dedicated) conduit'.

opts.d: ownPipe = true on the string; it may share the chase but never a pipe. Untick per circuit.
Packed by the capacity rule with the others.

questions.q: Preferred kötődoboz: how far does it pull a departure? ⚑
questions.why: A departure (a circuit leaving a shared run) needs a box; a preferred KD nearby should take it.

opts.d: A departure within 600 mm of a preferred KD on the shared stretch moves into it.
Tighter; more suggested boxes.
Anywhere on the same wall face of the same room.

questions.q: Mandatory kötődoboz: what exactly is mandatory?
questions.why: It must change the routing, otherwise it is only a preference.

opts.d: Every path that passes its wall-face stretch enters it (pipes cut there), and departures on that room face move into it.

opts.t: At least one circuit uses it
opts.d: Only checked (CK-13), routes unchanged.

questions.q: A departure with no box nearby:
questions.why: Cables may leave a shared pipe only in a box.

opts.t: Suggest a KD in a table
opts.d: A 100×100 KD is suggested at the spot (gen:'tpo'); you tick and apply, or place your own preferred KD and re-run.
Listed as an error; you place every box by hand.

questions.q: Distribution runs: share pipes like the trunk?
questions.why: E5 today packs several circuits per pipe only on the trunk; distribution is one pipe per circuit. You asked that parallel circuits share a conduit.

opts.d: The capacity-based packing (In ≤ Iz·k, 1,5 mm² ≤ 2 circuits, ≤ 3 cables) on every run, trunk and distribution.
Distribution stays one pipe per circuit.

questions.q: How does the topology reach the autowiring?
questions.why: The 'one engine' rule (E5-Q5: bundle, don't port).

opts.d: plan.js takes cfg.topo: explicit links replace its inference for those circuits; everything after (legs, packing, sizing, checks) is reused. One engine for the CLI and the page.

opts.t: A second router in the view
opts.d: The view routes and sizes on its own; the engine stays as is. Faster to build, two answers to the same question.
